Structural damage identification via physics-guided machine learning: a methodology integrating pattern recognition with finite element model updating
top_cited_works.abstract: Structural health monitoring methods are broadly classified into two categories: data-driven methods via statistical pattern recognition and physics-based methods through finite elementmodel updating. Data-driven structural health monitoring faces the challenge of data insufficiency that renders the learned model limited in identifying damage scenarios that are not contained in the training data. Model-based methods are susceptible to modeling error due to model idealizations and simplifications that make the finite element model updating results deviate from the truth. This study attempts to combine the merits of data-driven and physics-based structural health monitoring methods via physics-guided machine learning, expecting that the damage identification performance can be improved. Physics-guided machine learning uses observed feature data with correct labels as well as the physical model output of unlabeled instances. In this study, physics-guided machine learning is realized with a physics-guided neural network. recent_works.title: LES-based quantification of turbulence intensity effects on the wind pressure on low-rise elevated buildings
recent_works.venue: Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics
recent_works.abstract: Elevated low-rise buildings are commonly used in oceanfront regions to reduce the impacts of surge, wave and flooding. However, the complex wind effects on elevated houses remain unclear. Turbulence intensity is one of the essential factors that affect aerodynamic pressures on elevated houses, which, however, is not well addressed in existing references. This research attempts to quantify the effects of turbulence intensity on aerodynamic pressures on low-rise elevated houses using large eddy simulation (LES). Based on a validated LES model, the wind turbulence intensities are varied by 10% to 30% in streamwise and spanwise directions and three wind directions are considered. The resulting pressure fluctuations are analyzed in terms of mean, root-mean-square (r.m.s.), and peak values to characterize the aerodynamic behavior of elevated low-rise buildings under varying turbulence intensities. Research results demonstrate that while the time-averaged mean and r.m.s. pressure statistics are insensitive to moderate turbulence variations, the peak pressure coefficients exhibit high sensitivity. recent_works.title: Optimal replenishment schedule considering time value for logistic demand
recent_works.abstract: In recent years, due to the rapid advancement of technologies, more and more innovative products and skid products are introduced to the markets. As the life cycles of such products are shorter than those of durable goods, the effectiveness of their inventory management is therefore more critical to their competitiveness. Traditional inventory planning models and techniques mostly deal with products with long product life cycle. The assumption on the demand pattern and subsequent solution approaches are generally not suitable for dealing with products with short product life cycle. It is observed that in consequence of the imitation effect, the number of buyers is influenced by each other; the dynamic of the demand can thus be modelled with the logistic substitution model typically used for modelling imitation effects. In this research, one-inventory replenishment problems based on the logistic demand model are formulated and solved to facilitate the management of products with short product life cycle. Training Precoder and Combiner Design for Compressed Sensing Based Millimeter Wave Channel Estimation
recent_works.abstract: The training precoder and combiner for compressed sensing based millimeter wave channel estimation is investigated under the theory of compressed sensing. As the measurement matrix with small mutual coherence is required to efficiently employ the channel sparsity, we obtain the training precoder and combiner by means of minimizing the mutual coherence of the resulting measurement matrix for improving the channel estimation performance. Firstly, the training precoder and combiner design is formulated as a discrete combinatorial optimization problem. Then, a genetic algorithm based optimization method is proposed to solve this problem so as to minimize the mutual coherence of the measurement matrix. Simulation results verify that the precoder and combiner obtained by the proposed method can provide a measurement matrix with a small mutual coherence and the normalized mean square error of channel estimation using the obtained precoder and combiner can be improved.
